item.title: Deep-time Sediment Sulfur Isotopes (DSSI): a database of sedimentary sulfur isotopic records through Earth history
item.description:
Deep-time Sediment Sulfur Isotopes (DSSI): a database of sedimentary sulfur isotopic records through Earth history
Wenyi Guo, Huyue Song, Yong Du, Thomas J. Algeo, Jing Li, Hui Zhang, Junjie Xue, Jianwei Peng, Xiangpeng Ke, Haijun Song, Daoliang Chu, and Li Tian
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-610,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Sedimentary rocks preserve chemical clues to how Earth's oceans, atmosphere, and life have changed. We assembled a global, open database of chemical signatures of sulfur in marine sediments, spanning more than four billion years. Each entry records the material measured, its age, location, and source study. This resource helps researchers compare evidence across time and place to investigate long-term changes in ocean chemistry and Earth's environment.

item.title: A 30-Year satellite based climatological dataset of Antarctic Cloud Mass Meridional Transport events
item.description:
A 30-Year satellite based climatological dataset of Antarctic Cloud Mass Meridional Transport events
Jonathan M. Chambers, Matthew A. Lazzara, Hannah Zanowski, David E. Mikolajczyk, Sophie Orendorf, Taylor Ziegler, and Linda M. Keller
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-664,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
A 30-year dataset was made using infrared satellite data from November 1992–December 2022 to track the time, duration, and location of Cloud Mass Meridional Transport events (CMMTs). These events bring substantial heat and moisture poleward to Antarctica. CMMTs occurred more often during austral winter (JJA) and in regions such as Ellsworth Land in West Antarctica and Queen Maud Land in East Antarctica. The average number of CMMTs per year increased while their average duration decreased.

item.title: The European Geostrophic Wind Reconstruction (EGWR): a 220-year daily record of European geostrophic wind from surface pressure (1806–2026)
item.description:
The European Geostrophic Wind Reconstruction (EGWR): a 220-year daily record of European geostrophic wind from surface pressure (1806–2026)
Stephan Paul
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-755,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Spatially consistent European wind records span only about forty years, too short for rare, prolonged low-wind spells. We reconstruct daily large-scale wind for fourteen European regions back to 1806 from historical surface-pressure data, corrected per region to match modern ERA5. The 220-year record is validated against independent wind measurements and power generation, carries uncertainty and reliability information, and is openly available for studies of wind variability and wind droughts.

item.title: High-Resolution Above-Ground Biomass Mapping of the Alps using Satellite Embeddings and GEDI
item.description:
High-Resolution Above-Ground Biomass Mapping of the Alps using Satellite Embeddings and GEDI
Anna Candotti and Enrico Tomelleri
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-798,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
This study mapped forest biomass across the European Alps for the year 2022 to improve carbon storage estimates. By combining satellite data with space-borne laser measurements using machine learning, we created maps at high spatial resolution. These results provide a reliable tool for climate monitoring and forest management.

item.title: ArborVerse: Scaling Fine-Grained Urban Tree Species Classification to Millions of Trees Worldwide
item.description:
ArborVerse: Scaling Fine-Grained Urban Tree Species Classification to Millions of Trees Worldwide
Jiapeng Li, Yingjing Huang, Fan Zhang, Shengli Tao, Zhen Dong, Jun Yang, and Yu Liu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-380,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Street trees make cities healthier and more livable, but global research has been limited by scarce shared data. We created StreetTree, a public collection of over 12 million street-level images covering more than 8,300 tree species in 133 countries. Tests show that current image classification methods still struggle with real street scenes, where trees can look alike, change with seasons, and appear in varied conditions. StreetTree can support tree mapping, planning and greener city management.

item.title: A paired marine-fluvial modern pollen dataset from the Bohai Sea and its inflowing rivers, China
item.description:
A paired marine-fluvial modern pollen dataset from the Bohai Sea and its inflowing rivers, China
Jie Li, Shixiong Yang, Siyuan Ye, Xiangjun Meng, Xiaohui Chen, Xi Mei, Maosheng Gao, Qian Hao, Xianyong Cao, Bin Chen, Sangheon Yi, and Guangming Zhao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7661–7677, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7661-2026, 2026
To better read past landscape and climate changes from seafloor sediments, we built a paired record of plant pollen and spores from 430 Bohai Sea samples and 104 river samples from 16 rivers. The results show that pine pollen is more common in deeper, offshore areas, while grasses and salt-tolerant plants are more common near coasts and river mouths. This open dataset helps researchers judge how rivers, wind, and water depth shape the plant signals preserved in sea sediments.

item.title: Tongji-GMMG2025C: A High-Resolution Global Gravity Field Solution Integrated from Heterogeneous Gravity Data via a Grid-based VCE Method
item.description:
Tongji-GMMG2025C: A High-Resolution Global Gravity Field Solution Integrated from Heterogeneous Gravity Data via a Grid-based VCE Method
Jianhao Xuan, Qiujie Chen, Yunzhong Shen, Xingfu Zhang, and Yun Xiao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-646,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We developed a new high-resolution global gravity field model by integrating satellite, marine, terrestrial, airborne, polar, and topographic gravity information. The model substantially improves gravity estimation accuracy in coastal, polar, and data-sparse regions. Accuracy improves by 9 %–24 % within 10 km of the coastline and by approximately 40 % over Antarctica. The dataset can be used for geodesy, oceanography, and other Earth science applications.

item.title: An integrated wildfire event database for improved fire science research for the continental United States, 1992–2021
item.description:
An integrated wildfire event database for improved fire science research for the continental United States, 1992–2021
Eric S. Kasischke and Nancy H. French
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-660,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
A new wildfire event dataset was developed to improve information for studying wildfires in the continental United State for 1992 to 2021. It was created by integrating data from three existing datasets with information obtained from regional reports and datasets and reports found on the world wide web. For all United States regions, calculations using this new dataset increases total burned area, as well as the number of and burned  area in extreme wildfires (those larger than 5000 hectares).

item.title: A 1-km weekly dataset of floating Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri blooms in China’s marginal seas derived from multi-sensor satellite observations
item.description:
A 1-km weekly dataset of floating Ulva prolifera and Sargassum horneri blooms in China’s marginal seas derived from multi-sensor satellite observations
Mingqing Liu, Zhaotong Chen, Yingcheng Lu, Qianguo Xing, Jiaochan Hu, Haoyang Yu, Zhongbin B. Li, and Mengqiu Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-799,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Floating macroalgal blooms in China’s coastal seas can rapidly expand and spread, affecting marine ecosystems and human activities. This study developed a weekly dataset of two major floating macroalgae species from 2018 to 2025 using observations from multiple satellites. The dataset captures seasonal patterns, yearly changes, and rapid bloom dynamics, providing a consistent resource for understanding bloom development and supporting coastal monitoring.

item.title: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
item.description:
A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
Kwang-Sik Lee, Dong-Chan Koh, Young-Hee Kim, Won-Bae Park, Songyi Kim, Hyejung Jung, Yeon-Sik Bong, Woo-Jin Shin, Chaeyoung Kim, and Jeonghoon Lee
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7645–7659, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7645-2026, 2026
We present 462 paired measurements of stable oxygen and hydrogen isotopes in monthly precipitation from 15 sites on Jeju Island, South Korea, collected between 2000 and 2003. Isotope values were generally lower in summer and decreased with elevation. Published with weather data and sampling information, this historical dataset provides a baseline for future monitoring and supports research on groundwater recharge and the island’s water cycle.

item.title: Stable isotope bioarchaeological atlas from the post-Soviet space
item.description:
Stable isotope bioarchaeological atlas from the post-Soviet space
Anna Hagarová, Margarita Gorbulina, and Kévin Salesse
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-619,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Chemical traces in ancient bones and teeth reveal what people ate, where they lived, and how far they travelled. We compiled results from over a hundred studies, spanning more than one hundred thousand years across the former Soviet space, much published only in Russian and largely absent from international literature. The result is a large, open collection of ancient human and animal remains from Asia and the Caucasus, now freely accessible to researchers worldwide.

item.title: EU-wide maps of grassland management using 2022 LUCAS grassland and extended grassland data
item.description:
EU-wide maps of grassland management using 2022 LUCAS grassland and extended grassland data
Julien Morel, Jon Olav Skøien, Momchil Iordanov, Mattia Rossi, Matteo Marcantonio, Xavier Rotllan-Puig, Linda See, and Marijn Van der Velde
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-640,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Grasslands cover large parts of Europe and provide many services. Using the LUCAS survey, a large field survey covering the whole European Union, we produced the first regional map based on harmonized field data on grassland intensity and use, their forb-to-grass ratio, and age category. Strong differences in grassland management were found across Europe. This dataset can support satellite-based monitoring and large-scale modelling of grasslands.

item.title: GDNat: a global, daily, high-resolution, natural-forcing only temperature data set for attribution research
item.description:
GDNat: a global, daily, high-resolution, natural-forcing only temperature data set for attribution research
Robert Fofrich Navarro, Kelly E. McCusker, Steven B. Malevich, and Robert E. Kopp
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-658,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created a global daily temperature dataset showing what temperatures from 1979–2020 might have looked like without human-caused climate change. We combined historical weather records with climate model estimates of human influence while preserving real-world weather patterns. The dataset allows researchers to quantify the influence of human-caused climate change on observed temperatures in the historical record.

item.title: TORRENT: An observation-constrained and benchmark-ready community shared dataset in the contiguous United States for flash-flood research and model intercomparison
item.description:
TORRENT: An observation-constrained and benchmark-ready community shared dataset in the contiguous United States for flash-flood research and model intercomparison
Songkun Yan, Mengye Chen, Jonathan J. Gourley, Jian Zhang, Günter Blöschl, Paul Bates, Zhi Li, Siyu Zhu, Abigail Snooks, Yixin Wen, Xiaodong Chen, Chengbin Deng, Juan Camilo Parra Toro, Meihong Ma, and Yang Hong
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-695,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Flash floods develop quickly, but the records needed to study them are scattered across many sources. We created TORRENT by linking flood reports, rainfall, river flow, drainage-area information, and field measurements across the contiguous United States. It contains 42 466 reported events and 806 ready-to-use case packages, including 21 carefully checked cases. Its open, machine-readable design will help people and artificial intelligence tools study floods and compare prediction methods.

item.title: Trans-Atlantic aerosol transport from January to March 2025 – measurements from two expeditions on a research vessel
item.description:
Trans-Atlantic aerosol transport from January to March 2025 – measurements from two expeditions on a research vessel
Andebo Waza, Konrad Kandler, Franz Kanngießer, Julia Gottschall, Arne Leuzinger, Simon Speith, Natalia Sudarchikova, Sebastian Wahl, Wirginia Hepert, and Stephanie Fiedler
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-733,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Originating from North Africa, mineral dust, which is one of the most abundant aerosol types in the Earth’s atmosphere, is frequently transported across the Atlantic Ocean. To observe these dust transport different instruments, which provide information on both near-surface dust and lofted dust plumes, were deployed during two research cruises between January and March 2025 in the Atlantic Ocean. The presented data allows us to address existing knowledge gaps in trans-Atlantic dust transport.

item.title: TailWeather: from tail to extremes, a global climatological dataset for machine-learning weather forecasting
item.description:
TailWeather: from tail to extremes, a global climatological dataset for machine-learning weather forecasting
Zhi-Song Liu, Michael Boy, and Risto Makkonen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-792,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Weather forecasts are mostly judged on ordinary days, not on the rare heatwaves, cold spells, storms, downpours, and droughts that cause most harm. We built a global daily record of such unusual weather over land since 1981 and compared it with reported disasters. Rarer weather was more often linked to harm, but disaster records miss much of the world. Leading artificial intelligence forecasts often missed extremes, especially strong winds, so forecasts need testing on extremes everywhere.

item.title: Merge Satellite and Gauge Daily Precipitation Data for Areas with Sparse-Gauge and Rugged Terrain: A High-Accuracy Gridded Dataset CGS01 (2000–2024) across China
item.description:
Merge Satellite and Gauge Daily Precipitation Data for Areas with Sparse-Gauge and Rugged Terrain: A High-Accuracy Gridded Dataset CGS01 (2000–2024) across China
Bokun Yan, Wenpeng Li, Fuping Gan, Yuejun Zheng, Juan Bai, Longfeng Wang, Jianrong Li, Yi Guo, Chunyan Li, Naichen Xing, Yue Zhuo, and Ruoyi Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-564,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
This study constructs a new daily precipitation dataset covering China from 2000 to 2024. By integrating satellite and ground rainfall records with a robust, physically based calculation method, this new dataset overcomes the shortcomings of traditional products. Notably, it only utilizes 27 percent of the ground observation stations required by previous datasets, yet achieves substantially higher accuracy.
